title: Double the radius, not the volume
hook: Two ideal cylinders have equal height and radii of 3cm and 6cm.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Predict cylinder capacity scaling when radius doubles at fixed height.

misconception: Doubling radius only doubles an ideal cylinder’s capacity.
objective: Predict cylinder capacity scaling when radius doubles at fixed height.

claims.text: Ideal cylinders have inner radii 3cm and 6cm; both have inner height 10cm. Scaled model; ideal cylinders; V=πr²h; 1000cm³/L.

claims.text: Cylinder capacity depends on radius squared. Doubling radius multiplies the circular base area by four; equal height then gives four times the volume. The dimensions here are ideal internal measurements.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. claims.text: Two ideal cylinders have equal height; one has radius 4cm and the other 12cm. How many times as much does the wider one hold? Correct: 9. Capacity scales with radius squared: three times the radius gives 3² = 9 times the base area and volume.
